22 Unit 8 · Applications of Integration Standard [1 mark]
The graph of a function f′(x)f'(x)f′(x) is shown below. It is given that f(x)f(x)f(x) is a function such that f(1)=5f(1) = 5f(1)=5. The area between the curve y=f′(x)y = f'(x)y=f′(x), the x-axis, and the vertical lines x=1x = 1x=1 and x=5x = 5x=5 is represented by the shaded region. If the area of the shaded region is 16 square units, determine the value of f(5)f(5)f(5).
A. 999
B. 111111
C. 212121 ✓
D. 171717
Correct Answer: (C) — 212121
The area of the shaded region is given by the definite integral of f′(x)f'(x)f′(x) from x=1x = 1x=1 to x=5x = 5x=5. This area is also equal to the change in the function f(x)f(x)f(x) over this interval: ∫15f′(x) dx=f(5)−f(1)\int_{1}^{5} f'(x) \, dx = f(5) - f(1)∫15​f′(x)dx=f(5)−f(1).

The graph shows that the function f′(x)f'(x)f′(x) is a constant function, represented by the horizontal line y=4y = 4y=4. Therefore, f′(x)=4f'(x) = 4f′(x)=4.

The area of the shaded region is given as 16 square units.
Using the definite integral: ∫154 dx=[4x]15=4(5)−4(1)=20−4=16\int_{1}^{5} 4 \, dx = [4x]_{1}^{5} = 4(5) - 4(1) = 20 - 4 = 16∫15​4dx=[4x]15​=4(5)−4(1)=20−4=16.
This confirms the given area.

Now we use the relationship f(5)−f(1)=16f(5) - f(1) = 16f(5)−f(1)=16.
We are given that f(1)=5f(1) = 5f(1)=5.
Substituting this value, we get f(5)−5=16f(5) - 5 = 16f(5)−5=16.
Solving for f(5)f(5)f(5): f(5)=16+5=21f(5) = 16 + 5 = 21f(5)=16+5=21.

39 Unit 2 · Differentiation — Definition and Fundamental Properties Standard [1 mark]
The graph of a differentiable function f(x)f(x)f(x) is shown below. The tangent line to the graph at x=1x=1x=1 has the equation y=2x+ky = 2x + ky=2x+k. Given that f(1)=3f(1) = 3f(1)=3, determine the value of kkk.
A. 444
B. 111 ✓
C. 222
D. 333
Correct Answer: (B) — 111
The equation of a tangent line to a function f(x)f(x)f(x) at a point (a,f(a))(a, f(a))(a,f(a)) is given by y−f(a)=f′(a)(x−a)y - f(a) = f'(a)(x - a)y−f(a)=f′(a)(x−a). We are given that the tangent line at x=1x=1x=1 has the equation y=2x+ky = 2x + ky=2x+k. The slope of this tangent line is $2$, which means f′(1)=2f'(1) = 2f′(1)=2. We are also given that f(1)=3f(1) = 3f(1)=3. Substituting these values into the point-slope form of the tangent line equation:
y−3=2(x−1)y - 3 = 2(x - 1)y−3=2(x−1)
y−3=2x−2y - 3 = 2x - 2y−3=2x−2
y=2x−2+3y = 2x - 2 + 3y=2x−2+3
y=2x+1y = 2x + 1y=2x+1
Comparing this to the given tangent line equation y=2x+ky = 2x + ky=2x+k, we can see that k=1k=1k=1.

Alternatively, since the point (1,f(1))(1, f(1))(1,f(1)) lies on the tangent line, we can substitute x=1x=1x=1 and y=f(1)=3y=f(1)=3y=f(1)=3 into the equation of the tangent line:
3=2(1)+k3 = 2(1) + k3=2(1)+k
3=2+k3 = 2 + k3=2+k
k=3−2k = 3 - 2k=3−2
k=1k = 1k=1.
